result.title: Look, Reason, Draw a Region: Recursive Refinement for Spatial Context Prediction
result.summary: Spatial context prediction requires visual grounding and spatial reasoning to identify vacant regions relative to objects in a scene. Spatial relationships and physical constraints remain challenging for large vision-language models (VLMs). Recursive reasoning has demonstrated strong performance on discrete and abstract reasoning tasks, motivating its use for improving spatial context prediction in natural images. Weight sharing enables higher accuracy with a small trainable parameter count. We introduce Spatial-TRM, a compact recursive model with frozen vision-language features, a convex region decoder, and just 11.2M trainable parameters. This weight-tied reasoner supports six spatial relationships, three reference frames, and open-vocabulary anchor objects. On the RoboSpatial-Home benchmark, Spatial-TRM achieves 29.51% context accuracy, a gain of 9.02 percentage points (44.0% relative) over a separately trained single-step model with the same parameter count. Including the frozen encoders, the model has 877.8M total parameters, approximately $15\times$ fewer than the reported 13B size of RoboPoint. These results show that repeated refinement improves spatial context prediction from pretrained vision-language features at a fixed trainable parameter count on this benchmark.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Spatial-TRM：以冻结的视觉-语言特征配上凸区域解码器，构成一个仅 11.2M 可训练参数的权重共享递归模型，通过重复细化预测场景中相对物体的空间上下文区域，在 RoboSpatial-Home 上比同参数的单步模型提升 9.02 个百分点。
AI.relevance_reason: 权重共享的递归细化直接对应 LVR 关注的「loop 式推理状态生成与更新、动态计算收益」，其冻结编码器加轻量递归头的设计可供核查递归深度如何在固定参数量下保留视觉与几何证据；但输出是空间区域而非通用 latent 推理，需进一步确认其内部状态表示与使用方式。
